name: draft_four_walls
why: The benchmark of the draft: a 100x100x20 block, the front face as neutral, the four side faces inclined by 5 degrees. It is the case that the refusal of swapped faces leans on.
_why_the_faces_and_not_the_feature: The feature, when the angle is requested, ALWAYS declares what it was asked -- even when it has inclined nothing. Measured on 16/9/2026: swapping the selection marks, `IDraftFeatureData.Angle` reads back 5 degrees while the side faces stayed at zero. So here we count the faces of the PART that are at the right angle, and the angle declared by the feature is reported next to it, with a note saying what it is.
_why_the_volume_grows: Neutral on top and walls that widen towards the bottom: the frustum of a pyramid is bigger than the prism. 207080.74 against 200000. The number is not round and could not be: it is the integral of a section that changes with height.

expect.why: THE NUMBER WE START FROM. A straight block has no face at 5 degrees from the neutral: if it had one, the later count would no longer say anything.

HERE THEY COINCIDE, and in the broken case they coincide just the same: that is why it is not a check. It is in the answer to show that the two numbers are two different things, not to guarantee anything.

expect.tolerance_why: it is the volume of a frustum of a pyramid minus a prism: the calculation has a tangent inside
the same number read from the state instead of from the answer

expect.why: drafting tilts the walls, it does not break the part
